headline: Highest risk is medium: Plane can ingest and act on Awesome Selfhosted content, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error paths; data leakage and compliance risks are limited by the profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plane can ingest file uploads and hyperlinks, while awesome-selfhosted is a curated knowledge source that may contain attacker-controlled links or descriptions. Because Plane has no browser but does process files/links, the pair creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes severity up from low.
conditions: IF Plane imports content from awesome-selfhosted links or uploaded files into task text without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF an operator manually copies list entries from awesome-selfhosted into Plane notes, prompt injection can propagate.
mitigations: Disable automatic import of external list content into Plane.
Strip instructions and markup from imported entries before saving.
Use a review-only staging note for copied content.
Train operators to treat repository text as untrusted.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels for imported items.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge-management list with no touched data classes, while Plane touches issues, tasks, files, images, hyperlinks, and notes and can egress broadly. There is no shared workspace or secret-handling evidence, so a direct leakage path is not established. The main risk is limited to accidental disclosure through copied content or uploaded files.
conditions: IF sensitive material is pasted from Plane into awesome-selfhosted-derived notes, it may be exposed.
IF Plane file uploads contain confidential data and are later shared externally, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in Plane notes or uploads.
Redact sensitive fields before copying content between systems.
Restrict sharing of imported notes to approved users.
Review upload permissions in Plane.
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on uploads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Awesome-selfhosted has no write or network capabilities in its profile, while Plane cannot write the filesystem but does support multiple instances and broad network egress. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator or shared mutable resource not shown here, so the pair is mostly non-overlapping.
conditions: IF both agents are attached to the same mutable external resource through an unlisted orchestrator, conflicts can arise.
IF Plane instances are manually coordinated against the same task set without locking, race conditions may occur.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate resources.
Avoid shared writable directories.
Use a single writer for any shared task queue.
Check for duplicate Plane instances before bulk updates.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared backends.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane can turn imported content into issues, tasks, or notes, so if awesome-selfhosted-derived text is treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into work products. Awesome-selfhosted is a static knowledge list, not a verifier, so Plane should not trust it without review. The pathway exists in default usage when operators copy content across.
conditions: IF Plane uses copied entries from awesome-selfhosted as source-of-truth tasks, downstream mistakes can propagate.
IF operators rely on list text without verification, Plane may schedule incorrect work.
mitigations: Require human verification before creating tasks from imported text.
Mark imported items as untrusted until reviewed.
Separate source notes from actionable tasks.
Add a checklist step for factual validation.
requires-engineering: enforce provenance checks in task creation.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or certification mismatch is documented for awesome-selfhosted, and Plane's profile shows broad egress plus file uploads but no specific regulated-data handling. Because the pair lacks explicit compliance constraints, only a low-risk gap exists around accidental handling of sensitive notes or files. The other agent is not cited for a residency issue because none is stated.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Plane uploads or notes, compliance review is required.
IF an operator uses the pair for EU PII or PHI without a documented policy, a compliance gap may arise.
mitigations: Do not store regulated data in Plane by default.
Review retention settings before use.
Limit uploads to non-sensitive files.
Document the data class allowed in the workflow.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
